parole.significato: Used to form the plurals of some nouns.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Middle Low German [Term?]. Reinforced by the fact that French and English also use -s as a plural suffix.
Borrowed from Middle Low German vlōte, which pertains to fließen (“to flow”). The contemporary form is modelled on French flotte.

From Middle High German helle(n)barte, from older helmbarte, from helm (“stalk”) + barte (“axe”). The modern -d- is Central and Low German (compare Middle Low German hēlenbārde) and/or influenced by French hallebarde, itself from the Middle High German. The stress pattern, too, may hint at French in
Middle Low German, perhaps from French charte.

Borrowed from Middle Low German suppe, soppe, sope, which spread under the reinforcing influence of French soupe. Both from Proto-Germanic *supô, *suppô, *suppǭ (“broth, sop”), which is related to German saufen (“to drink”).

From taugen (“to be of use”) + nichts (“nothing”), alteration of older tügenicht (1548), itself perhaps after Middle Low German dögenicht (1514); compare Dutch deugniet (1539). The two earliest High German attestations are apparently in authors from the Low German borderland: 1548 in Burkard Waldis
